chunks: Ḥammād narrated to us from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) about the saying of the general Muslims: that the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) said, “Whoever dies while he has no Imam dies a death of Jāhiliyyah.” So he said: “It is true, by Allah.” I said: “If an Imam dies and a man in Khurāsān does not know who his successor is, does that excuse him?” He said: “It does not excuse him. When the Imam dies, the proof of his successor falls upon those who are with him in the town, and the duty of setting out belongs to those who are not in his presence when the news reaches them.”

Surely Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “So why should not a group from every party among them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them, so that they may beware?”
I said: “If a group sets out and some of them die before arriving and coming to know?” He said: “Allah, Majestic and Mighty, says:”
“And whoever goes forth from his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah.”

I said: “If some of them reach the town and find your door closed to you and your curtain let down, while you do not call them to yourself, and there is no one to direct them to you, then by what would they recognize that?” He said: “By the revealed Book of Allah.” I said: “How does Allah, Mighty and Majestic, say it?” He said: “I see that you have spoken about this before today.” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Then recall what Allah revealed concerning ʿAlī (عليه السلام), what the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) said to him concerning al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn (عليهما السلام), what Allah singled ʿAlī (عليه السلام) out with, and what the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) said regarding him from his bequest to him and his appointment of him, what would happen to them, the acknowledgment of al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn of that, his bequest to al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn’s submission to him by the word of Allah:”
“The Prophet has a greater claim over the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers; and those of kinship, some of them have a greater claim over others in the Book of Allah.”

I said: “The people have spoken regarding Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), and they say: how did it pass over, among the sons of his father, one who had kinship like his and one who was older than him, and come short of one younger than him?” He said: “The possessor of this matter is recognized by three qualities not found in anyone else: he is the worthiest of people in relation to the one before him, he is his successor, and with him are the weapons of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and his bequest. That is with me, and I am not disputed regarding it.” I said: “That is concealed out of fear of the ruler.” He said: “It is never in concealment except that it has an evident proof. My father entrusted to me what was there, and when death came to him he said: ‘Call witnesses for me.’ So I called four men from Quraysh, among them Nāfiʿ, the mawlā of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar. He said: ‘Write: this is what Yaʿqūb bequeathed to his sons:”
“O my sons, surely Allah has chosen for you the religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims.”

I said: “And Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī bequeathed to his son Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, and ordered him to shroud him in his cloak in which he used to perform the Friday salat, to wrap him with his turban, to make his grave squared and raise it four fingers, then leave it.” So he said: “Fold it up.” Then he said to the witnesses: “Depart, may Allah have mercy on you.” I said after they had departed: “What was there in this, O my father, that you had witnesses to it?” He said: “I disliked that you should be overpowered and that it should be said, ‘He did not leave a bequest,’ so I wanted there to be a proof for you. Thus, when a man comes to a town and says, ‘Who is the successor of so-and-so?’ it is said, ‘So-and-so.’” I said: “If he associates another in the bequest?” He said: “Ask him, for he will clarify it for you.”

key_terms.إِمَامٌ: the divinely appointed Imam whose recognition is obligatory
key_terms.النَّفْرِ: setting out or traveling in order to seek religious knowledge
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةِ: the bequest or testament indicating transfer of authority
key_terms.بِكِتَابِ اللَّهِ الْمُنْزَلِ: through the revealed Book of Allah as a means of recognition
key_terms.حُجَّةُ: the binding divine proof or authoritative evidence
key_terms.سِلَاحُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم weapon as a sign of rightful succession
key_terms.مِيتَةً جَاهِلِيَّةً: a death resembling the state of pre-Islamic ignorance

ai.seo_question: How is the true Imam recognized after the death of the previous Imam according to al-Kāfī?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the necessity of recognizing the Imam and explains that ignorance of the Imam after the death of the previous Imam is not an acceptable excuse once the means of knowing are available. It describes that the Imam is known through divine proof, prior designation, and inherited signs such as the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم weapon and bequest, while also citing Qur’anic verses about seeking religious understanding and lawful succession.
